mechanics.body_shape: read one 4-byte word out of the receiver and return it. No branch, no arithmetic, no flag write, no call, no write to memory, no stack traffic

byte_decode.0x8B: MOV r32, r/m32. A 32-bit load: four bytes of memory, one read, and it sets no flag. No prefix byte can be involved, because this is the first byte of the body, so the operand and address sizes are the 32-bit defaults
byte_decode.0x41: ModRM. mod = 0b01 so exactly one disp8 follows; reg = 0b000 = EAX; r/m = 0b001 = ECX. No SIB byte, no index, no base other than ECX
byte_decode.0x6C: the disp8, +108. Non-negative and one byte wide, so the addressed field is inside the receiver at +0x6c and can never be past +0x7c. This is the only address the function forms and the only constant in the body
byte_decode.0xC3: RET, with no immediate byte behind it because the body ends here

receiver_displacement.0x6c: the single displacement this body uses, decoded from the ModRM/disp8 pair and cross-checked against abi_derived.receiver.offsets ([108])

memory_reads.level: one: the dword sits at receiver+0x6c and its VALUE is the return value. Nothing dereferences the loaded word

validation.model_test: plain int main() with explicit checks, no framework and no external dependency. 100 checks in 10 cases. Layering: the header's kBodyBytes is the transcribed image and is itself asserted against literals (case K); the test contains an INDEPENDENT x86 decoder that walks the bytes, decodes the ModRM and disp8 itself, forms the address itself and logs what it read; re_00a649a0 is the code under test and shares no code with either of those. There are no callees to observe, so instead the test (a) asserts the absence of any call opcode from the bytes, and (b) feeds the decoder five deliberately altered bodies and requires it to reject each one, which is what makes 'no stack argument, no second operand, no call' an active claim rather than an assumption.
refutation_cases: A  displacement: decoy dwords at 0x60, 0x64, 0x68, 0x70 and 0x74 and a decoy byte at 0x6b, none of which may be the answer
B  access width: the field's four bytes are all distinct, so a byte load (0x12 at 0x6c, 0x34 at 0x6d, 0xcd at 0x6f) and a word load (0x3412) each answer something else
C  the receiver is read: the same object must answer differently after only the field changes, and two objects with equal fields must answer equally
D  the answer is neither the receiver pointer nor the address of the field

E  no width loss or normalisation: 15 values including 0x7fffffff, 0x80000000, 0x00000080, 0x000000ff, 0xdeadbeef and 0xffffffff, the last asserted as exactly 0x00000000ffffffff so a sign-extended or 64-bit-leftover result cannot pass
F  no write: every byte of the object and of the 16-byte guard band on each side is compared before and after, and the decoy dwords are re-read individually

G  no transfer and no flag writer: no E8/FF/9A and no EFLAGS-writing opcode anywhere in the 4 bytes, and the decoder rejects five altered bodies (a [ESP+4] read, a body with a CALL, a body with two NOPs, a RET 0x4, and MOVZX of the same displacement)
H  exactly one read, 4 bytes, at receiver+0x6c, agreeing with the reconstruction on every case
I  one level of dereference: the field is loaded with the address of a decoy block whose first dword is 0xfeedface, so a two-level read answers 0xfeedface and the correct answer is the address
K  the image: 4 bytes, 8B 41 6C C3, two instructions, a bare RET, and the decoded displacement is 0x6c
Q  the stack: 0 bytes of stack effect, measured by sampling ESP around the call through a thiscall shim, plus a compile-time assertion that the declared type is exactly Word(__thiscall*)(Receiver*)

The class name, the SDK name and the size of the real receiver. ghidra_function.sdk_name is null and the binary has no MSVC RTTI.

Branch polarity and signed-vs-unsigned compares, and write ordering against a callee. There is no branch, no callee and no write, and no such case was invented to pad the test out.

unresolved_questions: What the 4-byte word at receiver+0x6c is. The body, the seven verified vtable installations and the single caller give no name, no type and no nullability, and abi_derived's `pointer_like_in_EAX` is an INFERRED register class rather than a type -- recorded on its own in observed_original_abi.machine_return_class and deliberately kept out of observed_original_abi.return_type, since a register-class phrase is not a C or C++ type and no name in this package is derived from it. Whether the value really is pointer-like is itself open: nothing in these 4 bytes ever dereferences it, and the one caller stores it as an ordinary integer word. docs/analysis/residual-unknown-priority.md groups 0x00a649a0 with 0x005507a0, 0x005508c0, 0x005c0dd0 and 0x00ff3f00 as 'Local asset field projection' and says the open task is to bind one receiver field to a fixture-backed local metadata contract. Settling the name needs the class it belongs to, which needs RTTI this binary does not carry.

The vtable slot number, and therefore what a caller of this slot is asking for. The entry sits 0x88 = 34 dwords past the head at 0x013ff648, but whether that head dword is slot 0 is the convention this target does not settle, so the package declares no slot. Resolving it needs the RTTI complete-object-locator question settled for the Sporepedia vtable family first.

Whether the four neighbouring vtable runs the index lists (0x0147c9e8, 0x0147ca30, 0x0147ca70, 0x0147caf8 and the other heads in referenced_by_vtables) install a different function at the same position, or a different slot of this one. Only 7 of the 14 listed heads contain a dword equal to 0x00a649a0, and the three re-read for this package are among those 7; the rest were not read.

Whether the 4 bytes at +0x6c and the 4 bytes at +0x70 (which 0x00a649a8 reads, the next function in the image) belong to the same logical record. The adjacency is a fact and the grouping is a guess; nothing in this set joins them.

The class hierarchy this accessor belongs to. 0x005c0dd0 sits in the same vtable run 0x00a5 bytes away and appears in the same residual-unknown row, but no reconstruction package for it exists yet, so the shared receiver layout is unconfirmed from the other side.
known_blockers: FIELDS/OFFSETS (WARN, removed by repair rp04 2026-09-28; now PASS). The check reads the machine-derived receiver record as `bounds_only: true` (abi_derived.value.receiver: offsets [108], max_offset 108, written_through 0), which states how far the body was seen reaching and nothing about the identity of a word stored there, and it therefore WARNs whenever the target span NAMES a struct member. The span named one: `return receiver->field_6c;`. The displacement was never the problem -- the check itself reported the 1 displacement in that span as grounded within the receiver bounds (0x6c) and named the NAME alone as uncorroborated -- so the fix removed the name and kept the number. `struct Receiver` is now an opaque byte run, `std::array<std::uint8_t, 0xa4> opaque_00_a3`, with no member named anywhere; the single read is spelled `word_at(self, kFieldDisplacement)` with `kFieldDisplacement = 0x6c` a named constexpr pinned to the instruction by `static_assert(kFieldDisplacement == 0x6c, "MOV EAX,DWORD PTR [ECX+0x6C] at 0x00a649a0")` in sw1_00a649a0.cpp, and pinned a second time to the transcribed byte table by `static_assert(kFieldDisplacement == machine::kLoadDisplacement, ...)` in the model test. Both were verified to fire: re-valuing the constant to 0x70 stops the build. The access itself is byte-for-byte the same one -- base plus 0x6c, four bytes wide, one level of indirection, value returned and never dereferenced -- so no machine semantics changed. The 0xa4 run length is unchanged too, and it was already a test affordance (decoys at 0x60/0x64/0x68/0x70/0x74/0xa0), not a layout claim; no size is claimed for the real class. The two model-test uses of the member were rewritten to the displacement with identical values (`self + kFieldDisplacement` in case D, `word_at(f.receiver, kFieldDisplacement)` in case F), so no assertion was weakened: the suite is still 100 checks, still green, and the recorded +0x70 mutation still kills 43 of them (re-verified after the repair).

RETURN SEMANTICS (WARN, removed by repair rp04 2026-09-28; now PASS). The string-agreement arm compares the span's declared return type with the canonical `return_type` in the ABI record, and the two disagreed: the sidecar said `uint32_t` while the span declares `Word` (`using Word = std::uint32_t` in the types header). The span is the authority on what the source declares, so `observed_original_abi.return_type` now reads exactly `Word` -- the corpus spelling already used by e.g. pkg-swarm-w1-005ba0d0, which matches its own span. The 32-bit width this asserts is what the bytes support: the whole body is one `MOV EAX,DWORD PTR [ECX+0x6C]` plus a bare `RET`, and the single caller stores the result as the leading word of an integer record at 0x00a53dc0, which rules out a sub-word, a bool and a float return. The machine's register-class guess is recorded SEPARATELY, in `observed_original_abi.machine_return_class` = `pointer_like_in_EAX` with its own note, and is deliberately not spelled in `return_type`: a register-class phrase is not a C or C++ type, it is an INFERRED statement about the value class in EAX rather than a dereference, and no name in this package is derived from it. Whether that class is even right is added to unresolved_questions[0], which already said the phrase is not a type. `observed_original_abi.return_type_note` records the why of the exact spelling.
